title: Return the Factory
goal: Return a closure that retains its captured scale factor.
hints: Look at what happens to local variables when make_multiplier finishes executing.
A returning closure must take ownership of captured variables with move, and its type is written with impl Fn.
explanation: Returning a closure requires `move` so the closure takes ownership of `factor`. Without `move`, the closure attempts to borrow `factor` from a stack frame that is about to be destroyed, causing `E0373`. The return type must be written as `impl Fn(i32) -> i32` because every closure has an unnameable type. Writing `fn(i32) -> i32` fails with `E0308` because function pointers cannot store captured state. Bare `Fn(i32) -> i32` fails with `E0782` because traits are not concrete types.
